mainTopic: The width, strength, and shape of the קורה over a מבוי, and the 3:1 circle ratio learned from שלמה's ים
overview: The גמרא opens by asking how a קורה only one טפח wide can hold an אריח that is a טפח and a half wide. The answer is that plaster holds the extra half טפח in place. רבה בר רב הונא and רב חסדא then disagree about whether the beam's supports must also be sturdy. רב ששת rules that a beam covered by a mat hanging three טפחים off the ground counts as neither a קורה nor a מחיצה. A ברייתא follows with cases of beams that leave a gap, two thin beams side by side, and beams at different heights, along with the disputes of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רב corrects the משנה's wording to 'wide and sturdy' and explains that a beam four טפחים wide is a different case. The גמרא then explains why the משנה needed its lines about straw, curved, and round beams, including רבי זירא's rule for a curve that leaves the valid zone. Finally it proves from שלמה's ים that a circle three טפחים around is one טפח across, and begins working out the ים's volume, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why only one handbreadth if the brick is wider?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's minimum width of one טפח, because an אריח is a טפח and a half wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A handbreadth? It should need a handbreadth and a half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on the משנה. The משנה said the קורה needs to be one טפח wide, but the brick it must hold is wider than that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the beam must be able to hold an אריח, which is half of a לבינה. An אריח is a טפח and a half wide. So how can a beam only one טפח wide be enough to hold it?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara: A handbreadth?
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה's minimum width

phrases.english: It needs a handbreadth and a half!
phrases.notes: An אריח is 1.5 טפחים wide

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement that the קורה be one טפח wide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The beam must hold an אריח, which is 1.5 טפחים wide, so one טפח seems too narrow.

steps.title: The extra half handbreadth is held on with plaster
steps.stepSummary: A one-טפח beam is enough, because the leftover half טפח of the brick can be held in place with plaster on the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the beam is wide enough to hold one handbreadth, the remaining half handbreadth is fixed on with a little plaster on this side and a little on that side, and it stays in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The beam only has to hold most of the brick, and plaster takes care of the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam does not need to be as wide as the brick. One טפח of the brick sits on the beam. The extra half טפח sticks out and is held in place by a bit of plaster on each side, so the brick does not fall.

keyTerms.meaning: He fixes it on with plaster or clay

phrases.english: Since it is wide enough to hold a handbreadth,

phrases.aramaic: אִידַּךְ חֲצִי טֶפַח מְלַבֵּין לֵיהּ בְּטִינָא
phrases.english: the remaining half handbreadth he fixes on with plaster,
a little on this side
and a little on that side, and it stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical explanation: the משנה's measure works because of a simple building method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The beam must be as wide as the whole אריח, a טפח and a half
steps.terutzMaskana: One טפח is enough, because plaster holds the extra half טפח in place
steps.whatToRemember: The קורה must be one טפח wide. Plaster covers the gap for the rest of the אריח.

steps.title: Only the beam must be sturdy, not its supports
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that the קורה must be strong enough to hold an אריח, but the posts holding up the beam do not need to be that strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: The beam the חכמים spoke of must be sturdy enough to hold a small brick, but the beam's supports do not need to be sturdy enough to hold the beam and a small brick.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: how strong the beam and its supports must be. רבה בר רב הונא says only the beam itself has a strength requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים set a strength rule only for the קורה, since the beam is what makes the מבוי fit for carrying. The posts holding up the beam were not given any such rule. So weak supports do not ruin the קורה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, son of רב הונא
Small brick, half of a full brick
The supports that hold up the beam

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
The beam they spoke of must be sturdy
enough to hold a small brick,
but the beam's supports do not need

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בְּרִיאִין כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל קוֹרָה וְאָרִיחַ.
phrases.english: to be sturdy enough to hold a beam and a small brick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: from the beam's width to its strength
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the קורה must be strong enough to hold an אריח. Its supports have no such requirement.

steps.title: Both the beam and its supports must be sturdy
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees and rules that both the beam and its supports must be strong enough to hold a beam and an אריח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Both this and that must be sturdy enough to hold a beam and a small brick.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא argues with רבה בר רב הונא. He says the supports must also be strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, a strong beam is useless if what holds it up could not carry the load. So the posts must be able to bear the beam plus an אריח. This is a clear מחלוקת about the supports only.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Both this and that need

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בְּרִיאִין כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל קוֹרָה וְאָרִיחַ.
phrases.english: to be sturdy enough to hold a beam and a small brick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה בר רב הונא in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the קורה and its supports must be strong enough to hold a beam and an אריח.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת: רבה בר רב הונא requires strength only for the beam, while רב חסדא requires it for the supports too.

steps.title: A beam covered by a mat raised three handbreadths works as nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that if a mat is draped over the קורה and hangs three טפחים above the ground, it counts as neither a קורה nor a מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If someone placed a beam over an alleyway, draped a mat over it, and raised it three handbreadths off the ground, there is no beam here and no partition here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a new case and a ruling. A covered beam with a mat hanging down does not make the מבוי fit for carrying in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the mat helps twice: the beam is still there, and the mat looks like a wall. רב ששת says it fails both ways. The next step explains why.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
If he placed a beam over an alleyway,
and draped a mat over it
and raised it three handbreadths from the ground —

phrases.aramaic: קוֹרָה אֵין כָּאן מְחִיצָה אֵין כָּאן.
phrases.english: there is no beam here and no partition here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case about the קורה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קורה covered by a mat raised three טפחים off the ground works neither as a קורה nor as a מחיצה.

steps.title: Why it fails as a beam and as a partition
steps.stepSummary: The beam fails because it is hidden. The mat fails as a partition because goats can pass under a gap of three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no beam here, because it is covered. There is no partition here, because it is a partition that goats can pass through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each half of רב ששת's ruling, one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קורה works as a visible sign, so once the mat hides it, it does nothing. A מחיצה must reach close to the ground. A gap of three טפחים is big enough for young goats to pass under, so it does not count as a wall.
steps.confusionAlert: The text repeats 'קוֹרָה אֵין כָּאן' and 'מְחִיצָה אֵין כָּאן' on purpose. This is not a new ruling. The גמרא is now giving the reason for each half.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two basic rules: a קורה works only when it can be seen, and a gap of three טפחים under a מחיצה cancels it.

phrases.english: There is no beam here — because it is covered.
There is no partition here —

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ מְחִיצָה שֶׁהַגְּדָיִים בּוֹקְעִין בָּהּ.
phrases.english: because it is a partition that goats pass through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two parts of רב ששת's ruling in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hidden קורה does not work, and a מחיצה with a three-טפח gap below it does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: A covered beam is not a קורה, since it cannot be seen. A mat three טפחים off the ground is not a מחיצה, since goats can pass under it.

steps.title: A beam that does not reach across the alley
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if a beam, or two beams from opposite walls, leave a gap of less than three טפחים, no extra beam is needed. A gap of three טפחים does need another beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Suppose a beam sticks out from one wall but does not touch the other wall. Or suppose there are two beams, one sticking out from each wall, and they do not touch each other. If the gap is less than three, you do not need to bring another beam. If the gap is three, you do need to bring another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about a קורה that does not fully reach across the מבוי. It rules on how big a gap is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the קורה must span the whole entrance of the מבוי. Here the ברייתא says a small gap of less than three טפחים is treated as if it were closed. This is the rule of לבוד: a gap that small counts as joined. Once the gap reaches three טפחים, the beam no longer counts as complete, and you need another קורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our Rabbis taught.' This opens a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is outside the משנה.
A wall. Here it means one of the side walls of the מבוי.
The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as if it were closed.
Another beam, needed to fix the entrance of the מבוי.

steps.confusionAlert: The word לבוד does not actually appear in this text. It is the reason behind the three-טפח number, so you need to know it to understand why a small gap is allowed.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
A beam that sticks out from this wall
and does not touch that wall,
and likewise two beams,
one sticking out from this wall
and one sticking out from that wall
and they do not touch each other,
if the gap is less than three handbreadths,
phrases.notes: Less than three טפחים counts as closed, because of לבוד.

phrases.english: one does not need to bring another beam.
If it is three, one must bring another beam.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן קוֹרָה הַיּוֹצְאָה מִכּוֹתֶל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב ששת's case of a mat over the קורה to a new ברייתא about beams that do not fully reach across.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gap of less than three טפחים in the קורה is fine. A gap of three טפחים requires another beam.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a gap of up to four
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a gap of less than four טפחים is fine. Only a gap of four requires another beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if the gap is less than four, you do not need to bring another beam. If it is four, you do need to bring another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the תנא קמא about the same case of a beam with a gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions differ only on the size of the allowed gap. The תנא קמא says up to three טפחים. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the rule of לבוד works for any gap under four טפחים, so he is more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who often disagrees with the anonymous first opinion (the תנא קמא).
Less than four טפחים, his limit for a gap that still counts as closed.
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
if the gap is less than four handbreadths,
one does not need to bring another beam;
if it is four, one must bring another beam.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר פָּחוֹת מֵאַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same ברייתא, on the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gap of less than four טפחים is fine. A gap of four requires another beam.

steps.title: Two thin beams placed side by side
steps.stepSummary: Two thin beams lie side by side, and neither one alone can hold an אריח. If together they can hold one טפח of the אריח's width, no extra beam is needed. If not, another beam is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, suppose two beams are placed next to each other. Neither this one nor that one is wide enough to hold a brick. If together they can hold a brick across its width, which is one handbreadth, you do not need to bring another beam. If not, you do need to bring another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a second case: two thin beams placed next to each other. It rules on whether they can join together to count as one proper קורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a קורה must be wide enough to hold an אריח. Here neither beam is wide enough on its own. The תנא קמא says the two beams combine: if together they are one טפח wide, enough for the brick's width, they count as one kosher קורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two matching beams, placed side by side.
A half-brick, a טפח and a half wide and three טפחים long. The beam only has to hold one טפח of its width (see Step 2).
A handbreadth, a basic unit of measurement.

phrases.english: And likewise two matching beams placed side by side,
this one does not have enough to hold a brick
and that one does not have enough to hold a brick,
if together they can hold a brick across its width of one handbreadth,
one does not need to bring another beam;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: and if not, one must bring another beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא continues with a second case. This one is about the beam's width rather than its length.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two thin beams combine to count as one קורה if together they can hold an אריח across its one-טפח width.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires the brick's full length
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the two beams must be able to hold the אריח along its length of three טפחים. Otherwise another beam is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if they can hold a brick along its length, which is three טפחים, you do not need to bring another beam. If not, you do need to bring another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the תנא קמא about the two side-by-side beams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא was satisfied if the beams could hold one טפח of the brick's width. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל demands a measure of three טפחים, the brick's length. In this case he is the stricter one, even though he was the more lenient one in the gap case.

keyTerms.meaning: Three handbreadths, the length of an אריח.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has two disputes. On gaps: the תנא קמא allows less than three טפחים, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows less than four, so he is more lenient. On two thin beams: the תנא קמא needs only the brick's one-טפח width, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs its three-טפח length, so he is stricter.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is always the lenient one here. He is lenient in the first case and strict in the second.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
if it can hold a brick along its length of three handbreadths,
one does not need to bring another beam;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: and if not, one must bring another beam.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אִם מְקַבֶּלֶת אָרִיחַ לְאׇרְכּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion on the case of two side-by-side beams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams must be able to hold the אריח along its three-טפח length. Otherwise another beam is needed.

steps.title: One beam high and one beam low: picture them together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules that when two thin beams sit at different heights, we view them as if they were side by side. This applies only if neither beam goes past the valid height limits.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one beam was high and one was low, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: we look at the upper one as if it were lower down, and at the lower one as if it were higher up. This works only if the upper one is not above twenty אמות and the lower one is not below ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the case of two thin beams from Step 9. Now the beams are not side by side but at different heights, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says we may still count them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9 the beams lay next to each other, so they could hold the אריח together. Here they are far apart vertically. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses the idea of רואין, 'we view it as if,' and treats them as joined. His condition is that both beams stay in the valid zone: no higher than twenty אמות and no lower than ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it as if (we imagine the object in a different position)
רבי יוסי, son of רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: Both height limits use different units. The top limit is twenty אמות (cubits), and the bottom limit is ten טפחים (handbreadths). Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: If they were one above and one below,
phrases.notes: The two thin beams from the previous case

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאִין אֶת הָעֶלְיוֹנָה כְּאִילּוּ הִיא לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: We view the upper one as if it were below,
and the lower one as if it were above,
phrases.notes: So the two are pictured as joined together

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא עֶלְיוֹנָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
phrases.english: provided that the upper one is not above twenty cubits
and the lower one is not below ten handbreadths.
phrases.notes: Ten טפחים is the minimum height for a valid beam

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new variation: the beams are at different heights instead of side by side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two beams at different heights are viewed as joined, as long as the upper one is not above twenty אמות and the lower one is not below ten טפחים.

steps.title: אביי: the son agrees with his father about 'viewing as if'
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees with his father רבי יהודה on one point and disagrees on another. The point of agreement is that both use the principle of רואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds like his father in one thing and argues with him in one thing. He holds like his father in one thing, because he accepts the principle of 'we view it as if.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי compares the son's opinion to the father's opinion in the משנה. This step gives the first half of the comparison, the agreement, and sets up the disagreement for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a beam that is wide but not sturdy still works, because we picture it as if it were strong enough. That is רואין. His son uses the same imagination tool by picturing two separated beams as if they were together.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds like his father in one thing,
and argues with him in one thing.
He holds like his father in one thing —
in that he holds of 'we view it as if.'
phrases.notes: Like רבי יהודה in the משנה, who views a weak beam as if it were sturdy

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא analyzes the ברייתא from Step 11 by comparing it to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה agrees with רבי יהודה in using the principle of רואין.

steps.title: אביי: the son disagrees with his father about beams above twenty cubits
steps.stepSummary: The point of disagreement is height. רבי יהודה allows a beam above twenty אמות, but his son allows a beam only within twenty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he argues with him in one thing: רבי יהודה holds that a beam works even above twenty. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that within twenty it works, but above twenty it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his comparison by naming the one point where the son disagrees with the father: whether a beam higher than twenty אמות is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה allows a beam higher than twenty אמות. In Step 11, his son required the upper beam to stay at twenty or below. That condition shows he rejects his father's view on height.
steps.whatToRemember: The son agrees with his father that we may 'view it as if' (רואין). He disagrees on height: the father allows a beam above twenty אמות, and the son does not.

phrases.english: And he argues with him in one thing —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים,
phrases.english: whereas Rabbi Yehuda holds: even above twenty,
phrases.notes: A beam above twenty אמות still works

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds:
within twenty, yes,
above twenty, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא — דְּאִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's two-part comparison begun in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike his father, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not allow a beam above twenty אמות.

steps.title: רב יהודה teaches the משנה's line 'wide even if not sturdy'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. רב יהודה teaches this line to חייא בר רב while רב is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה says a beam that is wide is enough, even if it is not sturdy. רב יהודה taught this to חייא בר רב in front of רב: 'wide, even though it is not sturdy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and tells a short story of someone teaching it in front of רב. This step sets up the next step, where רב corrects the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's version is that a beam only needs to be wide enough for an אריח, even if it is too weak to actually hold one. רב יהודה repeats it word for word. Because רב is listening, we should expect a reaction.

keyTerms.meaning: Wide (wide enough to hold an אריח)
Sturdy, strong (able to actually bear the weight)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.aramaic: רְחָבָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּרִיאָה.
phrases.english: Wide, even though it is not sturdy.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda taught it to Chiyya bar Rav
in the presence of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: רְחָבָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּרִיאָה.
phrases.english: Wide, even though it is not sturdy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רְחָבָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּרִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the משנה. It is a new topic, separate from the ברייתא about two beams.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the version of the משנה being taught, רבי יהודה requires only that the beam be wide, not sturdy.

steps.title: רב corrects the wording to 'wide and sturdy'
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב יהודה to teach the line differently: the beam must be wide and sturdy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: Teach it to him this way: 'wide and sturdy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב rejects the version that was just taught and gives a corrected wording, which now requires the beam to be sturdy too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original wording said a wide but weak beam is enough. רב changes the text to 'wide and sturdy,' so a beam that is wide but too weak would not be enough. The next step challenges this from another statement of רב.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not adding a new opinion here. He is correcting the wording of the משנה as it was being taught.

phrases.english: He said to him: Teach it to him this way:
phrases.notes: רב speaking to רב יהודה

phrases.english: Wide and sturdy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects and corrects the wording taught in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The wording 'wide even though not sturdy' as taught by רב יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב, the correct text requires the beam to be sturdy as well as wide.

steps.title: רב seems to contradict himself about sturdiness
steps.stepSummary: רב just required the beam to be wide AND sturdy. But רבי אילעאי quotes רב saying a beam four טפחים wide is valid even if it is not sturdy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אילעאי say in the name of רב: if the beam is four טפחים wide, it is valid even though it is not sturdy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling from Step 15 by quoting a different statement of רב that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15 רב said the beam must be both wide and sturdy. Here רב is quoted as saying that width alone, four טפחים, is enough even without sturdiness. So which is it: is sturdiness required or not?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say! (opens a challenge from another statement)
An אמורא who transmits this teaching in רב's name
Sturdy (strong enough to hold a small brick)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elai say that Rav said:
If it is four handbreadths wide,
it is valid even though it is not sturdy!
phrases.notes: This sounds like a direct contradiction to רב's 'wide and sturdy' in Step 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's correction in Step 15 with another statement in his name.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement that the beam be both wide and sturdy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself is quoted as allowing a non-sturdy beam if it is four טפחים wide, so sturdiness seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A four-handbreadth beam is a different kind of case
steps.stepSummary: A beam four טפחים wide works for a different reason, so it does not need to be sturdy.
steps.simpleTranslation: A beam four טפחים wide is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. A beam that is four טפחים wide is treated differently from a regular beam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam four טפחים wide is so broad that it counts like a small roof (תקרה). We view its edge as coming down to form a real wall (פי תקרה יורד וסותם), so sturdiness does not matter. A narrower beam works only as a sign (היכר), and for that רב requires it to be sturdy.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different (a distinction between two cases)
The edge of a roof is viewed as coming down and closing off the space, like a wall

steps.confusionAlert: There is no real contradiction here. רב's 'wide and sturdy' is about a regular, narrow beam. The 'four wide' rule is a separate case, where the beam counts like a roof.

phrases.english: A beam four handbreadths wide is different.
phrases.notes: Such a beam is treated like a roof, not like a simple beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements of רב seemed to be about the same kind of beam.
steps.terutzMaskana: A regular beam must be wide and sturdy. A beam four טפחים wide counts like a roof and needs no sturdiness.

steps.title: Why mention a straw beam at all?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says even a straw beam is viewed as if it were metal. The גמרא asks what this adds, since the משנה already used the idea of רואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If it was of straw, etc.' What is this teaching us? That we say רואין, 'we view it as if'? That is the same as the earlier line!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the next line of the משנה, about a beam made of straw. It asks why this line is needed, since it seems to repeat something already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said a beam can be valid even if it is not sturdy, because we view it as if it could hold a brick. The straw line seems to teach the same idea of רואין again. So it looks like an extra, repeated line.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asks what a line adds)
We view it as if (we mentally picture it as valid)
That is the same as that (this repeats the earlier line)

phrases.english: [The משנה:] 'If it was of straw, etc.'
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה ends: 'we view it as if it were of metal.'

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
That we say 'we view it as if'?
That is the same as that earlier line!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the sturdiness discussion to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about a straw beam
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to repeat the earlier clause, which already used רואין for a non-sturdy beam.

steps.title: Straw teaches that רואין works even for a weak material
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought רואין applies only to a material that can be sturdy, like wood, and not to straw. The משנה teaches that it applies to straw too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we use רואין for a material whose own kind can be sturdy, but not for a material whose own kind is never sturdy. So the משנה teaches us that we use it here too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the straw line adds something new and is not a repeat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thin wooden beam is weak, but other wooden beams can hold a brick, so picturing it as sturdy is easy. Straw can never hold a brick, so we might have said רואין does not work for it. The משנה teaches that רואין works even for straw.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistake the line prevents)
Of its own kind (a material that can sometimes be sturdy)
Not of its own kind (a material that is never sturdy)

phrases.english: You might have said:
with a material of its own kind, we say it,
phrases.notes: For example, a weak wooden beam, since other wooden beams are sturdy.

phrases.english: but with a material not of its own kind, we do not say it.
phrases.notes: For example, straw, which can never hold a brick.

phrases.english: It teaches us [that we do say it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point (חידוש) by blocking a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רואין works only for a material that can sometimes be sturdy.
steps.terutzMaskana: רואין works even for straw, which can never be sturdy.

steps.title: A curved beam viewed as straight seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a curved beam is viewed as straight. The גמרא asks why this is needed, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A curved beam, we view it as if it is straight.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a curved beam, and challenges it as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam does not need to be perfectly straight, so a bent beam seems obviously fine. The challenge is: why would the משנה bother to teach something so simple?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (challenges a line as unnecessary)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up פְּשׁוּטָה ('straight', describing the beam) with פְּשִׁיטָא ('it's obvious!', the גמרא's challenge). They look alike but play different roles here.

phrases.english: [The משנה:] If it is curved, we view it
as if it is straight.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about a curved beam
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be no new point in saying a bent beam is acceptable.

steps.title: The curved-beam line teaches רבי זירא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The line is not obvious. It teaches the rule of רבי זירא, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us the rule of רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the curved-beam line teaches a real point. It is setting up רבי זירא's statement, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא only points to the source of the answer. The actual content, a case where the curve bends out of the valid zone, comes in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of רבי זירא

phrases.english: It teaches us in accordance with Rabbi Zeira.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the 'it's obvious' challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the line teaches a less obvious case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curved-beam line teaches only that bending is acceptable.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches רבי זירא's rule about a curve that leaves the valid zone (Step 22).

steps.title: רבי זירא's rule: mentally remove the part outside the valid zone
steps.stepSummary: If part of a curved beam bends out of the valid zone, we picture that part as removed. If the leftover gap is less than three טפחים, the beam is fine. If not, he needs another beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: the beam may be inside the מבוי while its curve is outside the מבוי. Or it may be within twenty אמות while its curve is above twenty. Or it may be above ten טפחים while its curve is below ten. In any such case, we picture the curve as removed. If the gap between the two valid parts would be less than three טפחים, he does not need another beam. If not, he needs to bring another beam.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains the case the משנה really means by a curved beam: part of the bend sticks out of the area where a beam counts. He gives the rule for when the beam still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A beam counts only inside the מבוי, below twenty אמות, and above ten טפחים. If the curve leaves that zone, that part does not count, so we picture it gone. If the two valid pieces left behind are less than three טפחים apart, we treat them as joined (לבוד) and the beam is valid. If they are three or more apart, there is a real gap, so he needs a new beam.

keyTerms.meaning: Above twenty אמות (too high for a beam)
Below ten טפחים (too low for a beam)
Three טפחים, the size of the gap that matters
The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed

steps.whatToRemember: A curved beam is viewed as straight only if, after picturing the out-of-zone bend removed, the valid pieces are less than three טפחים apart. If the gap is three or more, he needs another beam.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear example of רואין having limits. We may picture the beam as straight, but only when the real gap is small enough to count as closed under לבוד.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Zeira said:
If [the beam] is inside the alleyway
and its curved part is outside the alleyway,
or it is within twenty [cubits]
and its curved part is above twenty,
or it is above ten [handbreadths]
and its curved part is below ten,
we consider: in any case where, if its curved part were removed,
there would not be three handbreadths between this part and that part,
phrases.notes: Under לבוד, a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed.

phrases.english: he does not need to bring another beam;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא קוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: and if not, he must bring another beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of רבי זירא's rule that Step 21 pointed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If part of a curved beam is outside the valid zone, picture that part removed. If the remaining valid parts are less than three טפחים apart, the beam is valid. Otherwise he needs another beam.

steps.title: Isn't רבי זירא's rule obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's rule as obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי זירא's rule and says it is obvious. If we view the curved beam as straight, then of course we judge it this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said a curved beam is viewed as straight. So the גמרא asks what רבי זירא adds by telling us how to treat a part that bends away. This sets up the next step, which shows a case that is not obvious.

phrases.english: This too is obvious!
phrases.notes: Aimed at רבי זירא's rule from step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated by רבי זירא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule about the curved part of a beam
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems to follow automatically from the משנה's statement that a curved beam is viewed as straight.

steps.title: The case where the curve sticks out past the alley
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a beam inside the מבוי whose curve sticks out beyond it. We might have worried that people would carry along the curve outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for a case where the beam is inside the alley and its curve is outside the alley. You might have said: let us worry that people will be drawn to follow the curve and carry outside. So it teaches us that this is not a concern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא's rule matters in a special case: the beam sits inside the alley, but its curved part bends out past the alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case we might fear that people will follow the beam's curve and carry in the area outside the alley. רבי זירא teaches that we do not worry about this. We simply picture the outer part as removed, and the beam still works.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces the mistaken idea)

phrases.english: It is inside the alley
and its curve is outside the alley
for this case it was needed.
You might have said:
let us worry that perhaps
he will come to be drawn after it.
phrases.notes: He might carry outside, following the curve.

phrases.english: So it teaches us (that we do not worry).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the rule to a specific, non-obvious case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the beam is invalid because people would follow its curve and carry outside the alley.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about this. The beam is valid.
steps.whatToRemember: A curved beam is viewed as straight, even when its curve sticks out beyond the מבוי. We do not fear that people will carry outside.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention a round beam?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a round beam is viewed as square, and asks why it is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a round beam is viewed as if it were square. Why do I need this as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a round beam, and asks why it had to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has already taught the idea of רואין, picturing a beam differently than it really is, several times. So adding one more case of רואין seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need this as well?

phrases.english: A round one, we view it
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: as if it were square.
Why do I need this as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about a round beam
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea of רואין was already taught, so this clause seems repetitive.

steps.title: The real point is the measuring rule
steps.stepSummary: The clause is needed for its ending: a circumference of three טפחים means a width of one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The end part was needed: anything whose circumference is three טפחים has a width of one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the round beam case was written to teach the rule at its end, which tells us how wide a round beam is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam must be one טפח wide. For a round beam, the משנה gives a measuring rule: if it is three טפחים around, it is one טפח across. This new math rule is the reason the clause is there.

keyTerms.meaning: the end part of a teaching

phrases.english: The end part was needed:
anything whose circumference is three handbreadths
has a width of one handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The clause exists to set up a new rule in its ending
steps.terutzMaskana: A circumference of 3 טפחים equals a width of 1 טפח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the 3:1 ratio between the distance around a circle and the distance across it. The ratio is used for measurements throughout הלכה.

steps.title: Where does the 3-to-1 rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the ratio.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that three around equals one across.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack on the rule. It sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these words (what is the source)?

phrases.english: From where are these matters known?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the ratio of 3 around to 1 across

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: the ים that שלמה built
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן cites the פסוק about the ים: 10 אמות across and 30 אמות around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says, "He made the cast-metal sea, ten אמות from rim to rim, round all around, five אמות high, and a line of thirty אמות went around it."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers with a פסוק in מלכים about the huge round water basin that שלמה made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the basin was 10 אמות across and 30 אמות around. That is exactly three around for every one across, which is the source for the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: the 'sea', a giant basin in the בית המקדש
a cubit, a unit of length

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said,
the verse says:
"And he made the molten sea,
phrases.notes: מלכים א ז:כג

phrases.english: ten cubits from its rim to its rim,
phrases.notes: The width: 10.

phrases.english: round all about,
and its height was five cubits,
and a line of thirty cubits
phrases.notes: The circumference: 30.

phrases.english: went around it all about."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ים of שלמה was 10 across and 30 around, a ratio of 3:1.

steps.title: What about the thickness of the rim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof, since the rim's thickness could change the numbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is its rim!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's proof by pointing out that the basin had a rim with real thickness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one measurement was taken from the inside and the other from the outside, the rim's thickness would throw off the numbers. Then the 10 and the 30 would not show a clean 3:1 ratio. This sets up the גמרא's next move.
steps.confusionAlert: Here שְׂפָתוֹ means the rim's thickness. In the פסוק, "מִשְּׂפָתוֹ עַד שְׂפָתוֹ" refers to the edges used to measure the width.

phrases.english: But isn't there its rim?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's proof from the ים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rim's thickness means the two measurements may not match up, so the 3:1 ratio would not be exact.

steps.title: The rim was as thin as a lily petal
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the challenge about the rim's thickness: the פסוק says the rim was like a lily petal, meaning very thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: About its rim, the פסוק calls it 'the rim of a lily petal.' As it says: 'And it was a טפח thick, and its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like a lily petal. It held two thousand בת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the last challenge, that the rim's thickness would throw off the numbers. He shows from a פסוק that the rim was extremely thin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a thick wall would make the outside circle and the inside circle different sizes, so the 10 and the 30 might not belong to the same circle. רב פפא points out that the פסוק describes the rim as thin as a flower petal. The טפח of thickness was lower down in the body of the vessel, not at the top edge where it was measured.

keyTerms.meaning: Its rim or lip (the top edge of the vessel)
A lily blossom or petal, something very thin
A liquid measure used in תנ״ך

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׂפָתוֹ שְׂפַת פֶּרַח שׁוֹשָׁן כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Regarding its rim, it is written 'a rim like a lily petal,'
as it is written: 'And it was a handbreadth thick,
phrases.notes: מלכים א ז:כו

phrases.english: and its rim was made like the rim of a cup,
like a lily petal; it held two thousand bat.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שְׂפָתוֹ שְׂפַת פֶּרַח שׁוֹשָׁן כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 29 about the rim's thickness.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual reading of the פסוק: the rim was very thin
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rim had real thickness, so the inside and outside measurements would not belong to the same circle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rim at the top was as thin as a lily petal, so its thickness does not change the numbers in any real way.

steps.title: Even a thin rim has some thickness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: no matter how thin, the rim still has a tiny bit of thickness.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still a tiny amount of thickness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא. Even a petal-thin rim has some thickness, so the numbers still would not match exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא made the thickness small, but he did not make it zero. If we want an exact 1-to-3 ratio, even a tiny thickness means the inside and outside circles are not the same.

phrases.english: But there is still a minimal amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the thin rim solves the problem
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thin is still not zero. Any thickness at all makes the inner and outer circles differ, so the proof is still not exact.

steps.title: The circumference was measured from the inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 30-אמה circumference was counted along the inside of the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק counts the circumference, it counts from the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The 30 אמות were measured on the inside edge, so the rim's thickness does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both the width and the circumference are measured on the inside of the vessel, they belong to the same circle. The thickness of the wall is never counted. So the 10-to-30 ratio stays clean, and רבי יוחנן's proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof that a circle is 3 times its width holds up because the פסוק's measurements were all taken on the inside of the ים, so the rim's thickness never comes in.

phrases.english: When he calculates —
he calculates from the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא חָשֵׁיב — מִגַּוַּאי קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying how the measurement was taken
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 30 אמות might have been measured around the outside, which would include the rim.
steps.terutzMaskana: The circumference was measured on the inside, so the rim is not included and the ratio is exact.

steps.title: רבי חייא: the ים held 150 מקואות
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches in a ברייתא that the ים of שלמה held enough water for 150 מקואות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: The ים that שלמה made held the amount of 150 מקואות of purification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about how much water the ים held. This sets up a calculation about the ים's volume.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was the ים's width and circumference. Now רבי חייא adds information about its volume: 150 מקואות. The גמרא will next check whether this number fits with the measurements.

keyTerms.meaning: The huge water basin שלמה made for the בית המקדש
A מקוה, a ritual bath for purification

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
The sea that Solomon made
held
one hundred and fifty ritual baths of purification.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא: יָם שֶׁעָשָׂה שְׁלֹמֹה הָיָה מַחֲזִיק מֵאָה וַחֲמִשִּׁים מִקְוֵה טׇהֳרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ים's circumference to a new piece of data about its volume.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ים held enough water for 150 מקואות.

steps.title: How big is a מקוה?
steps.stepSummary: To work with רבי חייא's number, the גמרא asks how much water one מקוה holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, how much is a מקוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out the math behind רבי חייא's statement. It first asks for the size of one מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To turn '150 מקואות' into an actual amount of water, we need to know the size of one מקוה. This question is a setup for the calculation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (opens a reasoning step)

phrases.english: After all, a ritual bath, how much is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing the number given in Step 33.

steps.title: A מקוה is 40 סאה, with a source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a מקוה is 40 סאה, and begins quoting a ברייתא that proves it from the פסוק 'ורחץ את בשרו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forty סאה, as it was taught in a ברייתא: 'And he shall bathe his flesh…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the size of a מקוה, 40 סאה, and starts quoting the ברייתא that is its source. The quote continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have one piece of the math: 1 מקוה = 40 סאה, so 150 מקואות = 6,000 סאה. The ברייתא beginning with 'ורחץ את בשרו' will show where the Torah hints at 40 סאה.

'And he shall bathe his flesh,' the פסוק about immersion
